Metal is a conductor, which means electricity can flow through it easily. Glass is an insulator, which means it does not let electricity pass through. That is why electrical wires are made of metal and wrapped in plastic or rubber for safety.
Conductors allow electrons to move freely through the material, carrying an electric current.
Insulators block the flow of electricity and are used to keep people safe around wires.
